newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end down as bonds, dlr rally.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end down as bonds, dlr rally.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly lower in tune with soaring U.S. debt futures and a firm dollar after key U.S. jobs data.
Markets whipsawed after U.S. August jobs were reported up 250,000 and the jobless rate fell to 5.1 percent, with U.S. Treasuries tanking, then recovering to trade sharply higher.

The strong bonds, along with stocks, combined with expectations for a near-term U.S. rate increase to prop up the dollar much of the day. Currency futures saw moderate to heavy action, with many contracts breaking through recent ranges.
Traders called September yen's decline to a 7-1/2 week low orderly and the July 16 low at $0.009143 held losses.

September marks slipped to the lowest price in almost three weeks and Swiss francs were at the lowest price in 7-1/2 weeks, edging toward support at $0.8200. Canadian dollar resumed weakness seen on Thursday to post a double bottom at $0.7275 with the August 22 low.
By contrast, Mexican peso saw brisk buying interest that fueled a rally, and Australian dollar spend much of the day in fast market trading, vaulting to a fresh contract high at $0.8020.
Traders said bullish technical momentum carried Aussie through layer after layer of resistance, attracting stops and speculative interest.
Earlier comments from Reserve Bank Governor Bernie Fraser suggesting there was no need for a near-term Australian ease set off the buying frenzy.
"It was in a fast market all afternoon and it's been trading heavily," an IMM trader said. "Eighty cents was the big objective and it got there with some more to spare," he added.

September yen finished down $0.000023 at $0.009148, marks lost $0.0032 to $0.6704, Swiss franc fell $0.0081 to $0.8208, sterling fell $0.0060 to $1.5602, Canadian dollar ended flat at $0.7288, Aussie dollar rose $0.0069 to $0.8010, Mexican peso rose $0.001000 to $0.131600. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
